title: A larger ratio can hide missing observation
subtitle: Calculate with three original volume traces.
summary: Calculate with three original volume traces. Compare amount, interval-average flow and the effect of cropping an endpoint.

scope: Synthetic arithmetic with editorial time zero and piecewise-linear samples. Not patient data, spirometry quality certification, a validated clinical ratio or diagnosis.

passages.title: Name the quantity
passages.text: NHLBI distinguishes exhaled amount and speed in spirometry from lung-volume and diffusion testing. A quantity from one kind of test is not automatically a result from the others.

lenses.label: Amount and average flow
lenses.observation: Trace A rises by 2 L in its first 0.5 s.
lenses.question: Compute the interval-average flow and convert the amount to mL.
readings: The amount is 2000 mL; dividing 2 L by 0.5 s gives 4 L/s.
Trace B rises 1 L in the same interval: 2 L/s, although both full traces end at 4 L.
lenses.boundary: Amount and average flow have different units. Neither value is a health classification.

lenses.label: Keep the denominator visible
lenses.observation: The one-second amounts are 3 L and 2 L; the full authored endpoints are both 4 L.
lenses.question: What happens when the observed endpoint replaces the full one?
readings: A gives 3/4 and B gives 1/2. Cropped A gives 3/3.6 = 5/6.
The ratio rises after cropping because its denominator falls; this does not demonstrate improved physiology.
lenses.boundary: Label it volume at 1 s / observed end volume, not a certified clinical ratio.

lenses.label: Distinguish unknown from zero
lenses.observation: The cropped observation contains no sample after 2 s.
lenses.question: What would justify a claim about a complete clinical test?
readings: Additional measurements alone do not settle calibration, effort, time-zero and protocol quality.
A current technical standard and appropriate clinical evidence would be separate from the arithmetic here.
lenses.boundary: Do not extrapolate the crop, perform a self-test or infer disease.

activity.transfer: Create an arithmetic counterexample: keep a 1-second numerator fixed and lower the observed endpoint while keeping it above that numerator. Show why the ratio rises and list the observation you removed.
rubric: Keep amount, interval-average rate and dimensionless ratio distinct.
Use the explicitly authored samples and units.
Treat a cropped endpoint as incomplete evidence.
Do not interpret a synthetic ratio clinically.
